note: Three axes: technical domain x role function x organizational context. Job titles are aliases for combinations, and none of the axes produces a ranking. This file is where changes are made. The eight axes, two scales and four levels use the same values as the Mechanical Engineering Core: results from two majors can only be compared on the same ruler, and building a new ruler for each major would break comparison within a university

J1.name: Problem definition
J1.question: Who decided what to work on?

J2.name: Requirements interpretation
J2.question: Did you turn the requirements into numbers and constraints?

J3.name: Technical decisions
J3.question: Which items did you decide yourself?

J4.name: Methods and tools
J4.question: What did you use, and how?

J6.name: Comparison and verification
J6.question: What did you compare it against?

J7.name: Failure and correction
J7.question: How did you narrow down what went wrong?

J8.name: Organizational use
J8.question: Who used it, and for what?

S4.note: Screening scale. The four axes asked at BASIC. Organizational use is left out of screening because it puts undergraduates at a structural disadvantage: whether your work was used by an organization can only be answered if you were placed in one, and someone who has only done classes and a capstone will have that cell empty even if they made decisions. Organizational use is asked only in the in-depth stage

S8.note: Full scale. STANDARD and above. Do not use S8 as the denominator for S4. What the in-depth stage newly opens are the four axes not in screening (problem definition, requirements interpretation, methods and tools, organizational use)

levels.L1: Exposed. Watched or reused what someone else did
levels.L3: Owned. Decided it myself, and the result was used

technical_domains.name: Business Strategy and Planning
technical_domains.owns: Decides where to use resources and where not to use them

technical_domains.name: Marketing and Markets
technical_domains.owns: Decides what to tell to whom and through which channel

technical_domains.name: Sales and Business Development
technical_domains.owns: Offers and agrees on the terms of each deal and keeps a record

technical_domains.name: Financial and Investment Decisions
technical_domains.owns: Decides where to get money, where to put it, and the reasons

technical_domains.name: Accounting and Cost
technical_domains.owns: Records transactions by the standards and confirms them against the proof

technical_domains.name: Human Resources and Organization
technical_domains.owns: Decides the criteria for selecting, placing and evaluating people

technical_domains.name: Operations and Processes
technical_domains.owns: Decides the procedures that keep work running and the allocation of resources

technical_domains.name: Data and Decision-making
technical_domains.owns: Defines indicators and builds a basis for decisions from data

technical_domains.name: Customer and Service Operations
technical_domains.owns: Decides the steps customers go through, the service criteria and the range of exceptions

technical_domains.name: Demand, Reservation and Price Management
technical_domains.owns: Looks at the remaining quantity and time, and decides prices and allocation

technical_domains.name: Global Business
technical_domains.owns: Decides the rules, documents and exchange rate risk response for deals across borders

technical_domains.name: Information Systems and Business Requirements
technical_domains.owns: Turns work needs into tasks for a system and decides the scope of introduction

role_functions.name: Planning and Design
role_functions.output_kind: Business plan · Goals and indicators table · Reasons for priorities
role_functions.success: One plan that fits the resources and can be checked with indicators

role_functions.name: Analysis and Forecasting
role_functions.one_line: Looks ahead with numbers before a decision
role_functions.output_kind: Demand estimate · Profit and loss estimate · Indicator analysis report
role_functions.success: A basis that matches the results and changed a decision

role_functions.name: Verification and Audit
role_functions.one_line: Checks whether what was done is right
role_functions.output_kind: Reconciliation sheet · Proof check · Closing data
role_functions.success: A result where the numbers match the proof and the covered scope is written down

role_functions.name: Execution and Implementation
role_functions.one_line: Keeps work running again and again
role_functions.output_kind: Work procedure document · Schedule and role assignment · Spending records
role_functions.success: The same input gives the same result, and it can be reversed

role_functions.name: Customer Operations
role_functions.one_line: Keeps the customer side from stopping
role_functions.output_kind: Service criteria · Service quality measurement · Complaint handling records
role_functions.success: Within the promised level, and the same complaint does not come back

role_functions.name: Coordination and Negotiation
role_functions.one_line: Ties many people's decisions into one
role_functions.success: Rate of meeting the terms, and deadlines

role_functions.name: Market Exploration
role_functions.one_line: Narrows down things that have no answer yet
role_functions.output_kind: Research design · Market report · Test sales results
role_functions.success: The question is narrowed and a method remains

role_functions.name: People and Systems Management
role_functions.one_line: Makes sure standards are kept all the time
role_functions.output_kind: Job criteria · Evaluation criteria · Rule check records
role_functions.success: The same problem does not come back, and the basis of decisions can be traced

role_functions_note: There are eight, and they use **the same codes** as the Mechanical Engineering Core. Role functions are a layer above the major, so they are not created again for each major. All names were changed into business terms: `Design and Development` and `Test and Verification` are words for making things, so a student who does planning or accounting cannot find their place. The meaning of the work is kept the same, so the axes do not split; what differs is the kind of output: business plans, closing data and work procedure documents take the place of drawings

org_contexts.name: Finished Product and Brand Companies
org_contexts.performance: Sales and market share · Brand indicators · Operating profit
org_contexts.differs: My decisions come back right away as numbers in the market

org_contexts.name: Business-to-Business and Parts Companies
org_contexts.performance: Orders and on-time delivery · Unit price · Repeat orders
org_contexts.differs: The needs of one client company set the standard

org_contexts.name: Retail and Sales Channels
org_contexts.performance: Turnover and inventory · Profit by channel · Out-of-stock rate
org_contexts.differs: Looks at how fast things sell and how much stock is left, together

org_contexts.name: Public Institutions and Public Corporations
org_contexts.performance: Program goal achievement · Spending rate · Audit response
org_contexts.differs: Rules and set forms decide the schedule and the scope

org_contexts.name: Universities and Research Institutes
org_contexts.performance: Project performance · Report quality · Academic contribution
org_contexts.differs: You must show on your own that the method is right

org_contexts.name: Finance and Regulated Industries
org_contexts.performance: Soundness and meeting standards · Passing reviews · Audit records
org_contexts.differs: The traceability of the judgment is the output

org_contexts.name: Startups and small teams
org_contexts.performance: Sales and repeat purchases before the funds run out
org_contexts.differs: One person takes on several roles at once

boundaries.shared: Both are in roles that suggest a direction based on numbers
boundaries.a_difference: Decides where to use resources and takes responsibility for it
boundaries.b_difference: Is responsible for the indicators and comparison conditions that support that decision
boundaries.a_question: Have you decided a budget or staff allocation yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set the definition of an indicator and the comparison conditions yourself?

boundaries.a_difference: Decides in groups what to tell to whom
boundaries.b_difference: Sits face to face and agrees on the terms of each deal
boundaries.a_question: Have you chosen segments and channels yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you offered deal terms such as a discount or a delivery date yourself?

boundaries.a_difference: Estimates future money coming in and going out, and makes decisions
boundaries.b_difference: Records what has already happened and matches it with the proof
boundaries.a_question: Have you made an investment payback period or a funding plan yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you checked yourself whether the numbers match the proof?

boundaries.pair: Operations and Processes vs Customer Service
boundaries.a_difference: Handles throughput and errors through procedures and resource allocation
boundaries.b_difference: Handles the customer's experience and the service criteria
boundaries.a_question: Have you changed a procedure to reduce processing time?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set the service criteria or the range of exceptions yourself?

boundaries.shared: Handles at what price to sell
boundaries.a_difference: Changes prices by looking at the remaining stock and time
boundaries.b_difference: Decides what message to give to whom
boundaries.a_question: Have you looked at the remaining quantity and changed prices or allocation?
boundaries.b_question: Have you changed messages and channels and compared the responses?

boundaries.shared: Handles the conditions in which people work
boundaries.a_difference: Sets the criteria for selecting, developing and evaluating people
boundaries.b_difference: Allocates the order and amount of work those people do
boundaries.a_question: Have you set evaluation or hiring criteria yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you divided schedules and roles yourself?

boundaries.a_difference: Turns work needs into tasks for a system
boundaries.b_difference: Builds a basis for decisions from collected data
boundaries.a_question: Have you turned work needs into a list of features?
boundaries.b_question: Have you defined an indicator and extracted it from data?

boundaries.a_difference: Meets conditions such as rules, documents and exchange rate risk
boundaries.b_difference: Agrees on terms with the other side and makes the deal
boundaries.a_question: Have you chosen the rules that apply and the set of documents yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you agreed on price and delivery terms yourself?

boundaries.a_difference: Records by the standards and closes the books
boundaries.b_difference: Narrows down which activity the cost comes from
boundaries.a_question: Have you done account classification and closing adjustments yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you found and narrowed down yourself the activity where cost increased?

boundaries.shared: Works to keep the promised level
boundaries.a_difference: Solves the customer's problem on the spot
boundaries.b_difference: Changes the criteria so that the same problem does not come again
boundaries.a_question: Have you judged and handled an exception on site yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you changed the criteria or procedure to prevent the problem from coming back yourself?
